recentItems.title: How Do Fossils Form?: Crash Course Geology #18
recentItems.description:
Everybody dies, but few fossilize. In this episode of Crash Course Geology, we’ll learn how fossils form and why they’re so rare. Although very few living things ever become fossils, those that /do/ help us understand Earth’s history and how life came to be as it is today. 

Introduction: Nodosaur 00:00
What's a Fossil and How Do They Form? 0:31
Why are Fossils Rare? 5:15
What Can We Learn from Fossils? 6:30
Review and Credits 9:38

Sources: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RpwM8ZQPFk_DkzMJjMdtRrNGrJSNJ7FbgmQybSZ2Cqo/edit?tab=t.0

recentItems.title: How old is the Earth?: Crash Course Geology #17
recentItems.description:
What do iron deposits, fossils, and radioactive meteorites have in common? They’re all keeping records of our geologic history, the unimaginably long period of time that our Earth has been swinging around the sun. In this episode, we’ll look back into geologic time, discovering what we know, how we know it, and what it all means. 

Introduction: Michigan's Upper Peninsula 00:00
What is geologic time? 0:39
How do we study geologic time? 3:06
How old is Earth, and how do we know? 7:43
Review and Credits 10:34

Sources: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RpwM8ZQPFk_DkzMJjMdtRrNGrJSNJ7FbgmQybSZ2Cqo/edit?tab=t.0

recentItems.description:

But by studying and tracking seismic data, scientists continue to refine forecasts, better assess the risks, and even research how to prevent and protect us from the most damaging shocks.

recentItems.title: Is the Yellowstone volcano going to erupt again? 🌋
recentItems.description:
Yellowstone’s last supereruption was around 640,000 years ago, and geologists say there’s an “exceedingly low” chance that a supereruption would happen in the next few thousand years—  or possibly ever again. So don't worry. You can enjoy your Yellowstone trip in peace! 

To learn more about one of geology’s hottest creations — how they work, where they come from, and just how dangerous they really are— check out Crash Course Geology with @badnaturalist
